edges.description: Anti-PP1Pk binds transfused P/P1/Pk-positive red cells and drives complement-mediated intravascular haemolysis.

Transplacental IgG anti-PP1Pk is proposed to attack the globoside-rich fetal portion of the placenta. The mechanism is the standard explanation but is explicitly unproven; the relation between titre and loss risk is reported as unclear.
Where pregnancy continues, transplacental IgG binds fetal red cells, giving a positive cord direct antiglobulin test and usually mild haemolysis.

The human clinical burden is driven by the anti-PP1Pk isoantibody, and no murine isoantibody counterpart is reported, so the model is silent on haemolytic transfusion reactions, pregnancy loss and haemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn - which is to say, on everything that makes the human condition a disease.

nodes.description: The committed, non-redundant step of globo-series glycosphingolipid synthesis fails in the trans-Golgi network, so no Gb3 (Pk antigen, CD77) is made from lactosylceramide. No compensating glycosyltransferase exists.

evidence.reference_title: Human Gb3/CD77 synthase: a glycosyltransferase at the crossroads of immunohematology, toxicology, and cancer research.
evidence.snippet: Galabiosylceramide is the precursor of the gala-series, Gb3 initiates the globo-series, whereas P1 belongs to the neolacto-series of GSLs.

nodes.description: Two null A4GALT alleles - missense changes that abolish catalysis, nonsense variants, frameshifts or in-frame deletions - leave no functional lactosylceramide 4-alpha-galactosyltransferase. Alleles are highly heterogeneous between populations and often homogeneous within one, with p.Met183Lys predominant in Sweden, p.Pro251Leu and p.Trp261Ter in Japan and p.Ser100Leu among the Amish.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular basis for the p phenotype. Identification of distinct and multiple mutations in the alpha 1,4-galactosyltransferase gene in Swedish and Japanese individuals.
evidence.snippet: P251L and M183K mutations showed complete loss of enzyme function

genetic_context.description: Germline biallelic loss of function. Most reported probands are homozygous for a population-specific founder allele, but compound heterozygosity occurs and is not rare: a genotyping study of both P1PK and GLOB loci left eight p alleles unlinked because of it, and compound-heterozygous probands are reported. `zygosity` is deliberately left unset rather than recorded as HOMOZYGOUS, because the slot is single-valued and would otherwise assert the majority architecture as the only one.

nodes.description: Targeted disruption of the mouse Gb3/CD77 synthase gene deletes the globo-series glycosphingolipids completely, which is the same biochemical lesion as the human p phenotype. It is the model that demonstrates the receptor consequences of that lesion in a whole animal.

evidence.reference_title: Targeted disruption of Gb3/CD77 synthase gene resulted in the complete deletion of globo-series glycosphingolipids and loss of sensitivity to verotoxins.
evidence.snippet: To examine whether globotriaosylceramide (Gb3/CD77) is a receptor for verotoxins (VTs) in vivo, sensitivity of Gb3/CD77 synthase null mutant mice to VT-2 and VT-1 was analyzed.

nodes.description: Transplacental IgG anti-PP1Pk gives a frequently positive cord blood direct antiglobulin test. Clinically significant disease is uncommon and usually mild, managed with phototherapy where it occurs.

nodes.description: Transfusion of ABO-compatible but P/P1/Pk-positive red cells into a p individual with anti-PP1Pk causes severe, potentially fatal acute haemolysis. Only p red cells are compatible, which makes rare-donor registry access the central management problem.

evidence.snippet: The study underscores the critical need for rare donor registries, especially for patients at high risk of severe hemolytic reactions during transfusion.

nodes.description: Intravenous immunoglobulin is given alongside therapeutic plasma exchange in anti-PP1Pk isoimmunized pregnancy. In the best-documented case it was started with twice-weekly plasma exchange at 9 weeks of gestation at 1 g/kg, against a threshold titre of 16, and the titre fell from 128 to 8 by 10 weeks; the pregnancy reached term with an uncomplicated delivery and unremarkable newborn haemoglobin and bilirubin. The evidence is case-report level and the two treatments were given together, so the contribution of immunoglobulin on its own is not separable.

evidence.reference_title: Successful management of maternal anti-PP1P(k) alloimmunization in pregnancy with therapeutic plasma exchange and intravenous immunoglobulin.
evidence.snippet: Twice-weekly TPE (1.5 plasma volume [PV], 5% albumin replacement) with weekly titers and IVIG (1 g/kg) was initiated at 9 weeks of gestation

evidence.reference_title: Successful management of maternal anti-PP1P(k) alloimmunization in pregnancy with therapeutic plasma exchange and intravenous immunoglobulin.
evidence.snippet: With multidisciplinary care, a successful pregnancy is possible with IVIG and TPE adjusted to PV and titers.

nodes.description: Absent Gb3 deprives B3GALNT1 of its substrate, so globoside (Gb4, the P antigen) cannot be made, and the downstream GLOB-collection antigens are lost with it. The enzyme's second acceptor branch is lost in parallel, so the P1 antigen on paragloboside is absent too. Erythrocytes and tissues therefore display no Pk, no P and no P1 - the serological p phenotype. This is substrate-level epistasis on B3GALNT1, not a second mutation.

evidence.snippet: The P antigen is globotetraosylceramide (Gb4), produced directly from Pk (Gb3) (Fig. 2) and hence also absent in p individuals.

nodes.description: Individuals with the p phenotype form anti-PP1Pk (historically anti-Tj-a), with both IgM and IgG components, without prior transfusion or pregnancy. The initiating stimulus is not established; cross-reactive environmental Gal-alpha1,4-Gal glycans are the usual proposed explanation by analogy with the ABO isoagglutinins, but no primary study demonstrating the immunogen was found. Titre fluctuates and is boosted by transfusion and pregnancy.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical consequences of the extremely rare anti-PP1Pk isoantibodies in pregnancy: a case series and review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: Individuals with this phenotype spontaneously form anti-PP1Pk isoantibodies, associated with severe haemolytic transfusion reactions, recurrent spontaneous abortion and haemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn (HDFN).

nodes.description: Only p red cells are compatible, so management of any transfusion need depends on advance access to a rare-donor registry, family screening for p siblings, and where feasible directed or autologous donation. Elective surgery has been conducted without transfusion where compatible units could not be guaranteed.

nodes.description: Recurrent, predominantly first-trimester pregnancy loss in women with anti-PP1Pk is the dominant reproductive burden and a common route to ascertainment. No reliable quantitative loss risk could be sourced; the retrievable primary statements are qualitative, and the relationship between antibody titre and risk is reported as unclear.

evidence.snippet: The rare p phenotype in the rare PP1Pk blood group system is closely associated with spontaneous first-trimester abortions.

nodes.description: The P antigen (globoside) is the cellular receptor for parvovirus B19. Erythroid progenitors of p individuals lack it, and their marrow sustains normal erythropoiesis in the presence of very high virus concentrations. This is a demonstrated protective consequence of the genotype in humans, not an inference.

evidence.reference_title: Resistance to parvovirus B19 infection due to lack of virus receptor (erythrocyte P antigen).
evidence.snippet: People who do not have P antigen, which is the cellular receptor for parvovirus B19, are naturally resistant to infection with this pathogen.

evidence.reference_title: Resistance to parvovirus B19 infection due to lack of virus receptor (erythrocyte P antigen).
evidence.snippet: bone marrow from donors with the p phenotype maintained normal erythropoiesis despite very high concentrations of virus

nodes.description: Globotriaosylceramide is the receptor for Shiga toxin (verotoxin), so cells that cannot make it have no receptor to bind. This has been demonstrated in the Gb3/CD77 synthase-null mouse, which survives verotoxin doses lethal to wild-type animals. It has not been shown in human p individuals: no clinical study of Shiga toxin-producing infection in this population was found, so the human protection is an inference from the mouse and from the receptor biology, not an observation.

evidence.reference_title: Targeted disruption of Gb3/CD77 synthase gene resulted in the complete deletion of globo-series glycosphingolipids and loss of sensitivity to verotoxins.
evidence.snippet: Although wild-type mice died after administration of 0.02 microg of VT-2 or 1.0 microg of VT-1, the mutant mice showed no reaction to doses as much as 100 times that administered to wild types.

nodes.description: Plasma exchange, with or without intravenous immunoglobulin, is the mainstay of managing anti-PP1Pk isoimmunized pregnancy, aimed at lowering antibody titre. The literature is limited to a small number of case reports, and early initiation in high-risk women is what is advised rather than demonstrated in trials. Pregnancies are managed in a high-risk obstetric service with serial middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity Doppler to screen for fetal anaemia.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical consequences of the extremely rare anti-PP1Pk isoantibodies in pregnancy: a case series and review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: Early initiation of TPE in high risk patients should be strongly considered.

nodes.description: A compound-heterozygous genotype in a Chinese woman with the p phenotype and recurrent pregnancy loss, identified by whole-exome sequencing. It is recorded here as the worked example of the non-homozygous architecture.

evidence.reference_title: Novel A4GALT Variants Cause Rare p Phenotype and Recurrent Pregnancy Loss in a Chinese Individual.
evidence.snippet: Whole-exome sequencing revealed the presence of two compound novel heterozygous variants c.370_371del and c.507C>G in the A4GALT gene, which contributed to the p phenotype and pregnancy loss in this woman.
